benchmark.name: acquisition-workload-sweep
benchmark.scope: Local timing of the checked scalar, NEON, and available SME2 acquisition implementations; no performance conclusion is embedded in the report.
benchmark.execution_order: Fisher-Yates shuffle of every valid implementation/mode pair before each warm-up and timed sample block
benchmark.steady_state_definition: Prevalidated input, precomputed CFO weights, and preallocated implementation workspace; complete correlation, magnitude-squared scoring, and top-two reduction are timed.
benchmark.per_capture_definition: The acquisition plan and allocations are reused while prevalidated IQ windows are cycled. Every implementation reads contiguous timing grids directly from interleaved IQ; SME2 packing is timed only when a non-contiguous timing grid requires it.
benchmark.setup_inclusive_definition: Includes acquisition-plan allocation/CFO-table generation and checked execution; SME2 additionally includes output-workspace allocation and any input packing required by the timing grid.

fairness_contract.candidate_set: One shared timing/CFO hypothesis plan is used by every implementation.
fairness_contract.accelerated_precision: NEON and SME2 use bitwise-aligned float32 weights and float32 accumulation; the scalar oracle uses float64 weights and accumulation.
fairness_contract.scoring_and_selection: Magnitude-squared scoring and top-two candidate selection are included for every path.
fairness_contract.fallback_policy: An accelerated path is timed only when its reported implementation matches the requested path.
fairness_contract.target_isolation: Reference vectorization controls and accelerated target flags are source-specific; an SME2 build gives NEON a target with SVE and SME disabled.
fairness_contract.dead_code_control: Every timed block consumes a fingerprint of its final acquisition result through a volatile sink.

source_compile_flags.sme2_control: generic common flags; no SVE/SME target

memory_accounting.scope: Logical payload bytes unless the field explicitly names allocated capacity; allocator bookkeeping and stack objects are excluded.

limitations: Results describe one local process run and are not device-independent performance claims.
No CPU affinity, frequency locking, thermal stabilization, or energy measurement is performed.
Synthetic workload classes are engineering sweeps, not mission-derived waveform standards.
Steady-state timing includes score calculation and top-two selection; it is not an instruction-only microbenchmark.
Per-capture timing reuses the plan and allocations. SME2 reads contiguous timing grids directly and includes packing only for non-contiguous timing grids.
The setup-inclusive mode includes implementation-specific setup costs and is not expected to rank paths identically to steady state.
The scalar oracle accumulates in float64; NEON and SME2 use the same float32 weights and float32 accumulation and are correctness-gated against the oracle.
Reported memory is payload/capacity accounting, not process resident-set size or allocator overhead.
The historical Viterbi branch-metric experiment is independent and is not evidence for acquisition performance.
